title: Causes of World War One (KS3/4 History)
subject: History
strapline: Long-term tensions and the spark that lit them.
facts: Historians often group the long-term causes with the acronym MAIN: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, Nationalism.
Militarism: the great powers, especially Germany and Britain, built up huge armies and navies (a naval arms race).
Alliances split Europe into two armed camps: the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and the Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia).
Imperialism: rivalry over overseas empires and colonies increased tension between powers.
Nationalism: intense national pride and independence movements, especially in the Balkans, destabilised the region.
The trigger was the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary in Sarajevo on 28 June 1914.
The alliance system then pulled the powers into war one after another in the summer of 1914.

quick_quiz.q: What does the acronym MAIN stand for?

quick_quiz.a: the Triple Alliance and the Triple Entente

teacher_tips: Distinguish long-term causes from the short-term trigger clearly.
Use MAIN as a planning frame for causation essays.
Debate "which cause mattered most?" to build argument skills.
